title: I Logged Every Quick Favor My Sister-in-Law Texted During Dinner

parts.text: I sat down to meatloaf at 6:30 and my phone lit up: can you grab the kids from practice. Then: also the dry cleaning. Then: actually can you meal-prep Sunday. My sister-in-law, Paige, lived twelve minutes away and treated my calendar like a shared Google sheet she did not have access to. I was thirty-two. My brother shrugged. "She's overwhelmed." I started a note titled Paige Favors with timestamps. By dessert there were seven texts. I answered none of them. At 8:02 she called the landline. "Are you mad?" I said I was eating. She said family doesn't clock-watch. I screenshotted the thread and the meatloaf. Saturday she posted in the family chat that I had "abandoned the kids at soccer." The kids were with their dad, my brother, who had been on the couch the whole time. He looked at me. I looked at the note. It had become a spreadsheet.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: She accused me in the family chat while the kids were on the couch with their dad.

social.description: Dinner, a sister-in-law who outsourced parenting by SMS, and a spreadsheet that started as a note. Would you have answered the eighth text?

parts.text: I dropped the spreadsheet in the family chat with columns: time, ask, who was actually available. My brother was listed seven times as sitting ten feet from me. Paige typed that I was keeping receipts like a lawyer. I said I was keeping dinner. She demanded an apology for "public humiliation." I asked her to stop using abandoned as a word for a meal. My mom called it petty. I called it a log. The chat went quiet for three days, which is the longest it has been quiet since 2019. Paige now texts my brother first. I eat meatloaf with my phone in the other room. The spreadsheet still exists. I do not add to it unless someone tries to rewrite the evening.
